subject: Polity
description: Election, role as RS Chairman, removal

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is ELECTED by:

options.option_text: Electoral college of MPs + MLAs (similar to President)
Electoral college of ALL MPs of both houses — ELECTED + NOMINATED — of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha

questions.explanation: Art 66 — VP elected by Electoral College consisting of MEMBERS OF BOTH HOUSES of Parliament (including NOMINATED members — a key difference from President, whose electorate excludes nominated members). Single transferable vote, proportional representation.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Vice-President of India is the EX-OFFICIO:
questions.explanation: VP is Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Art 64). Not a member of RS (nor of Parliament). Presides over proceedings. When acting as President (temporary vacancy), he does NOT perform the RS Chairman role — Deputy Chairman does.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: A Vice-President can be REMOVED from office by:

options.option_text: A resolution of Rajya Sabha passed by EFFECTIVE majority, agreed by Lok Sabha

questions.explanation: Removal process simpler than President's. Art 67(b) — RS resolution passed by EFFECTIVE majority (majority of all current members), then agreed by simple majority in LS. No Article 61 impeachment procedure applies. Minimum 14 days' notice required.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The FIRST Vice-President of India was:
questions.explanation: Dr. S. Radhakrishnan — first VP (1952-62), subsequently 2nd President (1962-67). His birthday (5 September) is Teacher's Day in India. Rajendra Prasad was first PRESIDENT (1950-62). Zakir Husain and V.V. Giri were later VPs/Presidents.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The TERM of the Vice-President is:
questions.explanation: Art 67(a) — VP holds office for 5 years. Eligible for any number of re-elections (no limit). Term starts from day of taking charge; continues till successor takes charge. MINIMUM age: 35 years.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: When the PRESIDENT's office is VACANT, who acts as President?
questions.explanation: Art 65 — VP acts as President during vacancy (death, resignation, impeachment of President). Election for a new President must be held within 6 months. If VP also unavailable, CJI acts as President (happened 1969, Hidayatullah between Zakir Husain's death and V.V. Giri's election).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: In the Rajya Sabha, the CHAIRMAN (VP) has a vote:

options.option_text: Only in case of a tie (casting vote)

questions.explanation: Like the Speaker of Lok Sabha, the VP (as Chairman of RS) casts a vote only in case of a TIE. Maintains neutrality in regular proceedings.
questions.subject: Polity
